title: History-Dependent Skill-Induced Failure: Why the Same Skill Causes Different Failure Modes Across Tasks
frozen_required_unit: Use the released SkillsBench or SWE-Skills-Bench datasets to identify matched task pairs where the same loaded skill causes a Task-Implementation Fault in both tasks. Control for task-requirement-level compatibility and skill content. If the failure mode (IRF vs. RRO) is identical across all matched pairs, the context-sensitive uptake mechanism is falsified. If failure modes vary but are predicted by static compatibility alone, the mechanism is falsified.

current_upstream.semantic_role: Answers what the current author download chain contains; it is not substituted for the paper-time experiment snapshot.

provenance_basis.resolution: First-party dataset-versioning documentation identifies the retired original arXiv-v1 86-task paper snapshot as reproducible at commit adbaf4d7; this receipt resolves that short SHA to the full commit above.

paper_v1.semantic_role: First-party commit snapshot identified for reproducing the original arXiv-v1 paper task suite; this is distinct from the later/current 87-task roster.

snapshot_roster_comparison.conclusion: Current upstream is not a one-task extension of the paper snapshot; current identities must not be used to backfill paper-run joins.

skill_identity_semantics.conclusion: The receipts call these bundled curated skill IDs, not author-provided gold labels.

why_hold: Benchmark identity/provenance is no longer the blocker, and the existence of manual IRF/RRO truth is no longer uncertain. The first-party arXiv source for arXiv:2608.11888 states that each retained case was manually inspected, assigned one root-cause label, and finalized through group consensus; it fixes IRF=46 and RRO=36, and states that each paper run recorded the loaded skill and trajectory. However, the submitted arXiv source does not declare a project/code/data release URL or expose a row-level annotation table joining those manual labels to stable paper-run host-task and loaded-skill identities. Exact GitHub repository searches also did not locate such a release as of 2026-08-19, while unauthenticated GitHub code search was not executable and is not counted as a zero-result check. The frozen C02 falsifier therefore remains HOLD on public/reviewable case-level truth. Inferring IRF/RRO from task text, outcomes, heuristics, or an LLM would still replace the frozen truth source, and original SkillsBench trajectories must not be substituted for the harmful-paper runs without exact identity proof.
reopen_only_if: Reopen when a first-party case-level release, or an independently reviewed equivalent truth source, exposes the manually adjudicated IRF/RRO labels together with stable paper-run host-task and loaded-skill identities. A future public release should trigger re-audit; absence is asserted only as of the 2026-08-19 audit, not permanently.
